matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns overstating neural variability saturation and linear relationship claims in the Abstract of a tactile neuroscience paper. All findings relate to a federated learning paper about class-wise sampling and temperature scaling, addressing completely different scientific content.

GT 2 identifies a fabricated citation (Grant, 2025) about whisker hunting behavior in the Introduction. Finding 6 mentions fabricated references but in a federated learning paper's Related Work section, not about whiskers or tactile sensing.

GT 3 concerns inconsistency in whisker array arrangement (5×7 with zero padding for 30 whiskers) in the Method section. The findings discuss federated learning methods with no mention of whisker arrays or biological sensor configurations.

GT 4 addresses missing hyperparameter adjustments between two whisking datasets with different simulation frequencies. The findings discuss federated learning datasets (CIFAR, TinyImageNet) with no connection to physics simulation or whisking data.

GT 5 concerns selective reporting of neural alignment scores that inflate effectiveness in the Experiments section of a neuroscience paper. Findings 4, 10, and 14 discuss data integrity in federated learning experiments, but address different scientific issues (class-wise sampling, variance omission).

GT 6 identifies overgeneralization about tactile augmentations being critical and image augmentations causing training failure. Finding 8 discusses rhetorical manipulation but in the context of federated learning claims about class-wise sampling, not augmentation strategies.

GT 7 concerns omission of ethical reflection on tactile neural dataset scarcity in the Discussion. Finding 7 identifies ethical integrity omission but in a federated learning paper regarding privacy and consent, not neural dataset limitations.

GT 8 addresses misalignment between claimed maximal bite forces (8-10 N) and simulation clipping range (±1 N) in the Method. The findings discuss federated learning methods with no mention of force simulation or biological plausibility constraints.

GT 9 concerns missing hyperparameter details for SSL training stages in the Method section of a tactile processing paper. Findings 3 and 13 discuss experimental protocol issues but in federated learning contexts (replay buffer budgets, baseline tuning), not SSL training.

GT 10 identifies zero decoding accuracies in Table 6 (Appendix) for stimulus tasks where chance is 0.5 or 0.33, suggesting implementation errors. The findings discuss federated learning tables with no mention of stimulus decoding or chance-level performance issues.

GT 11 concerns incomplete IntersectionRNN update equations in the Appendix with undefined variables like y_t^ℓ. Finding 1 and 2 discuss method logic issues but for ISVD encryption and leverage scores in federated learning, not RNN update equations.

GT 12 identifies cross-section inconsistency between Abstract claims of saturating neural variance and Discussion acknowledgment of limited tactile datasets. Finding 9 and 15 discuss context misalignment but in federated learning contexts (sampling claims vs. limitations), not neural data.

GT 13 concerns overextending GPT-based attender results to suggest biological attention mechanisms in the Discussion. Finding 12 discusses claim distortion but regarding temperature scaling module effectiveness in federated learning, not biological attention.

GT 14 addresses failure to discuss biases from small sample (11 mice, 999 units) in the Discussion. Finding 7 identifies ethical omission but regarding privacy/consent in federated learning, not neural sample size limitations.

GT 15 concerns unbalanced comparisons between ConvRNN and baseline architectures lacking parameter count/compute budget controls in Experiments. Finding 3 and 13 discuss experimental design but for federated learning replay buffers and baseline tuning, not architecture comparisons.

GT 16 identifies neural fit scores exceeding maximum inter-animal consistency (1.34), suggesting overfitting or calculation errors in Experiments. The findings discuss federated learning performance metrics with no mention of inter-animal consistency or neural predictivity bounds.

GT 17 concerns fabricated claim of first neural comparison to rodent somatosensory cortex citing visual cortex papers in Related Work. Finding 6 identifies reference fabrication but in federated learning literature, not neuroscience comparisons.
